_comment: THE FAULT-KIND VOCABULARY, declared ONCE and shared by both cases.
A finding is judged to be OF A KIND when its text matches one of that
kind's regexes. This is half of the matching rule; the other half is the
part's own name. Neither half alone counts. See README.md -> The rule.
Regexes are Python re, matched case-insensitively against whitespace-
collapsed text. They are deliberately about the SHAPE of the complaint
(an icon too big, a label on two lines), never about a fault's identity,
so no regex here can be tuned to a particular run's wording.

wrapped-label: (label|text|caption|wording|title)[^.]{0,60}(wrap|wrapped|wrapping|two lines|2 lines|second line|second row|another row|another line|two rows|2 rows|three rows|3 rows|needs? (a |an )?(second|another|third|extra) (row|line)|onto (a|another) line|onto \d+ (lines|rows)|breaks? (onto|across|over))
missing-part: (missing|absent|not (present|there|built|rendered|found|in the build)|no such (button|control|element)|does not (exist|appear)|never (built|rendered|appears)|could not find)
(nowhere|not anywhere) (to be found|in the build|on the (screen|page))
month-mismatch: month[^.]{0,80}(is not the|isn't the|is different from the|does not carry|doesn't carry|did not carry|advances?|advanced|shift(s|ed)?|jump(s|ed)? (to|by))

_comment: A kind whose fault is a COMPARISON gets a named comparator here,
implemented in score.py. A regex cannot compare two measurements,
and the numeric floor that stood in for one (an icon is oversized
at 40px) was arbitrary: the real Lock month button's 34px icon in
a 32px control fell under it and scored 0.

Fix round 3 (F2): the icon vocabulary was the harness's own short list (icon/glyph/svg/chevron), so the identical sentence scored 1 with 'icon' in it and 0 with 'arrow' — and the build's Continue-to-builder icon IS an arrow. Widened generically to the words a person writes (arrow, symbol, graphic, image, mark, badge, artwork, logo, caret), bounded and pluralised so 'bookmark' and 'remarkable' are not icons. It cannot loosen a must-not-fire case: none of these words changes which way the comparison points.
